text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 4.5% today after hitting a low of $372.74 just three days earlier, recovering some ground from a brutal two-week slide of 17%. The rebound likely reflects stabilization following last week's sharp selloff—the stock had fallen nearly $58 from its early-November high—but also comes as oil prices ticked modestly higher (US crude at $99.64/barrel) and refineries continue running at a healthy 94.5% capacity, supporting margins for processors like Marathon.

The two-week decline itself looks tied to the company's late-October earnings announcement and likely concerns about policy shifts after the midterm elections. News that a Democratic Congress could favor renewable energy over fossil fuels, combined with earnings that may not have impressed investors, drove the initial retreat. Today's bounce is a technical recovery rather than a fundamental shift—the stock remains well below where it started the month.
